text:
Jordan (Acme): Hey team — since the reranker v2.1 rollout yesterday our support logs show a big spike in 'missing citations' tickets. The results are less grounded, worse recall for documents that used to appear in top-3. Example attached below. We're on a live workspace and it's impacting SLAs.  

Maya Chen: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a couple of failing queries + the responses you expect vs what you're getting now? Also which workload/route are you calling (api key/tenant)?

Jordan (Acme): Route is /v1/rerank with tenant acme-prod, token redacted. Example 1:
User query: "what policies apply to remote contractors in Q3 2023?"
Expected: cites doc IDs [doc_743, doc_129] with short excerpts. Now: returns generic paragraph and cites nothing; doc_743 used to be rank 1.

Jordan (Acme): Another quick repro:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
 -d '{"query":"renewal deadlines for enterprise contracts","top_k":10,"reranker_version":"v2.1.0"}'

Output snippet (current):
"top_hit": {"id": "doc_12", "score": 0.41, "snippet": "policy overview..."}  // no doc_84 which previously was top with clear citation

Raj Patel: Thanks Jordan. A couple of quick checks: did you also change the embedding model or index at the same time? Reranker alone shouldn't remove citations unless the upstream retrieval set changed or scoring thresholds were updated. Any change to embedding_model, index rebuild, or recall/top_k?

Jordan (Acme): No, embeddings are the same (embed-2024-bert-small). We didn't touch the index. Our logs show the rollout id: rollout/2025-06-rerank-v2.1.0 and it matches the deploy-bot message below.

deploy-bot: rollout complete — id rollout/2025-06-rerank-v2.1.0 by @raj at 2025-06-19T03:22:10Z. Canary -> 100% traffic.

Liam O'Connor: Pinged infra to pull traces. On our side I see an uptick in per-request tokenization time for reranker v2.1, but that wouldn't change recall. Raj any changes in loss weighting or negative sample strategy for v2.1?

Raj Patel: v2.1 changed the calibration of pairwise margin and introduced soft-negative mining with a lower margin (to reduce aggressive rerank demotions). It improved MRR on eval but could make precision lower in configs with small top_k. Jordan — what's your top_k in production?

Jordan (Acme): We set top_k=10 for reranker then truncated to top3 for display. Could that truncate useful diversity? It used to be fine with v2.0.

Raj Patel: Possible. v2.1's softer margin might compress scores so that after truncation you lose the formerly diverse picks. Two quick mitigation options: 1) increase top_k to 30 before truncation; 2) temporarily pin reranker to v2.0 while we bisect. Which can you do faster?

Jordan (Acme): We can increase top_k but it impacts cost. We asked for an emergency rollback of reranker on our tenant if possible.

Maya Chen: I've opened internal ticket CS-7894 and linked to customer case ACME-2219. Requested tenant pin to v2.0 for acme-prod. Triage notes: possible regression in reranker scoring distribution after v2.1; replicate on staging with acme query set.

Olivia Ruiz: I pulled traces for a sample request from acme-prod and correlated with per-request logs. No errors, but the reranker is returning lower score variance. Attached a tiny histogram:  (variance v2.0 = 0.18, v2.1 = 0.06). That supports Raj's compression hypothesis.

Jordan (Acme): Can you also check the citation pipeline? We rely on an assembly step that picks the highest-scoring doc and then extracts an excerpt. We're seeing the extractor run but no matching doc ids in the final message.

Raj Patel: That sounds like a downstream join bug is possible — if the reranker changed id formats or prefixes. Did doc ids change shape? Jordan, can you paste a raw response JSON from before and after (full ids)?

Jordan (Acme): Before (v2.0): top_docs: [{id: 'doc_84'}, {id: 'doc_743'}, ...]
After (v2.1): top_docs: [{id: '84'}, {id: '743'}, ...]  <-- OMG this is from our logs; some systems strip the 'doc_' prefix. Could the reranker output be returning numeric-only ids now?

Liam O'Connor: That's critical. I found a migration in the assembly layer where we added a numeric-only id normalization to support a new backend. Looks like the new normalization was toggled on in the rollout manifest by mistake. If the extractor expects 'doc_XXX' we will miss matches. This is a join mismatch not ML quality.

Maya Chen: So root cause might be a packaging/config change in the rollout, not reranker scoring. Raj/Eng — can you confirm timeline: normalization toggle flipped in rollout/2025-06-rerank-v2.1.0?

Liam O'Connor: Confirmed. The rollout manifest included 'id_normalization: numeric_only' flag to be toggled only for the new index backend but it propagated to all tenants. Reverting that flag for acme-prod should restore citations.

Raj Patel: Still want to check score compression, but fixing id join is highest priority. Jordan — we'll push a targeted config revert for acme-prod in the next 10 minutes and monitor.

deploy-bot: patch applied — rollout/2025-06-rerank-v2.1.0:acme-prod config revert 'id_normalization' at 2025-06-19T03:41:02Z.

Jordan (Acme): Thanks — I can confirm citations are back for the sample queries. We'll continue monitoring production for the next hour and report regressions. Huge thanks for the quick action. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: Follow-ups: 1) engineering to run a full regression test vs ACME query set in staging and report score distributions; 2) ML to run a small ablation on v2.1 to see if soft-negative mining still desirable; 3) product to add a pre-rollout checklist item to prevent config flags leaking across tenants.

Raj Patel: I'll schedule an internal postmortem and add the ablation tasks. Initial takeaway: two separate issues — id normalization bug (primary, fix applied) + potential score compression (investigate further).

Jordan (Acme): Appreciate the responsiveness. Please keep the ticket updated and CC our account rep.

Maya Chen: Will do. CS-7894 updated, linking to ACME-2219 and the deploy logs. Closing this thread once the hour monitoring window passes and customer confirms no more regressions.

Jordan (Acme): Confirming after 1h: looks stable. Staying on top_k 10 for now. Thanks again.

Liam O'Connor: Adding a short mitigation note in internal runbook — how to pin reranker version and override id_normalization per tenant.

Raj Patel: Postmortem draft next steps: timeline, root cause (config leak), detection (variance histogram + customer reports), remediation (config revert), and action items (pre-rollout checklist, tenant isolation tests, score calibration ablation).

Maya Chen: Marking as resolved for customer but leaving open for engineering follow-up. :white_check_mark:
